[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
aws_s3_bucket_policy.access_log_policy and aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block.access_log both reference only aws_s3_bucket.access_log, so they are created concurrently even though S3 validates PutBucketPolicy against the bucket's Public Access Block settings (block_public_policy / restrict_public_buckets). If the policy is written first, it can be accepted while the block is not yet in place, and enabling block_public_policy afterwards does not retroactively affect an existing policy. Add `depends_on = [aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block.access_log]` to aws_s3_bucket_policy.access_log_policy so the public access block is applied first.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`aws_s3_bucket_policy.access_log_policy` only references the bucket (`aws_s3_bucket.access_log[0].id`) and the policy document, so nothing forces the bucket-level Public Access Block to exist before the policy is attached. Both PUT Bucket ACL and PUT Bucket Policy behavior is governed by the Public Access Block settings (`block_public_policy`, `restrict_public_buckets`), so the public access block must be in place first — otherwise the bucket policy can be created (or later updated) while the bucket has no protection, and any policy that AWS evaluates as public will be rejected with AccessDenied. Establish the ordering with `depends_on = [aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block.access_log]` on `aws_s3_bucket_policy.access_log_policy`.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
resource.aws_s3_bucket_policy.access_log_policy attaches a policy to the access-log bucket while resource.aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block.access_log configures the bucket-level public access block for the same bucket, but neither references the other, so Terraform applies them in an unspecified order. If the bucket policy is applied before the public access block, AWS can reject the PutBucketPolicy call (with block_public_policy enabled) and the bucket temporarily lacks its public-access protections; the public access block should be established before the policy is attached.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
aws_s3_bucket_policy.access_log_policy attaches a policy to the access-log bucket, but has no ordering relationship with aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block.access_log, which sets block_public_policy = true on the same bucket. With no attribute reference or depends_on linking them, Terraform may apply the policy and the public access block in parallel or in the wrong order, causing PutBucketPolicy to be rejected or leaving the enforcement ordering undefined. The public access block should be created before the bucket policy is attached.
